prompt: Hard-sun on-model photograph, vertical 9:16, a full-bleed 9:16 photograph edge to edge with no borders, bands or panels: one forearm of a young Indian woman, warm wheatish skin, natural texture, raised upright 4 cm in front of a lime-washed saffron wall, elbow below the frame, the relaxed hand at the top, palm toward the wall, short bare nails, five fingers, correct anatomy; nothing else of her. The bangle sits above the wrist bone, both pave caps crossing at the front. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. It shows it worn at true scale: use reference 2 only for the piece, how it sits on the wrist and its true size there; take nothing else from it: not the person, her face, lips, clothes or background. LOCK: 1 continuous ribbed snake-coil wire, 4 mm thick, wound 2 full turns, 6 cm inside. The 2 ends pass at the front, so only there the stack is 3 wires deep (12 mm); elsewhere 2 (8 mm). Each end: 1 rectangular cap, 8 mm tall, rounded tip, 8 clear round pavé stones in 2 columns of 4; upper cap ends the top turn, lower cap the bottom, offset diagonally. 18k gold tone, high polish. Must stay 2 full turns with a short 3-wire overlap only between the caps, never 3 full coils or a stack of separate bangles. Both turns and both caps are the same 18k gold tone. PAVÉ AND CAPS, exactly as reference 1: each cap carries exactly 8 large round clear stones, 2 across and 4 down, in 4 rows of 2, each stone about 1.8 mm and almost half the cap's width, each in its own round setting with a thin line of gold tone metal between the stones; never 6 stones, never 3 rows, never a field of tiny micro-pavé. Each cap is a solid mirror-polished 18k gold tone block, twice as tall as the wire is thick and taller than it is long, with a rounded tip, as in reference 1; never a flat square plate with a raised frame. (Last time each cap became a flat, near-square plate with a raised bevel frame and only 6 stones, 2 columns of 3.) SCALE AND PROPORTION, as in reference 2: the wire is slim, 4 mm, about a quarter of the width of her index finger; the two turns together are 8 mm, as thick as a pencil and about half the width of her index finger; the bangle is about 17 wire widths across and its inside is wider than her wrist, so it sits loosely; never a chunky, fat or heavy coil, never a cuff; resting on the skin just above her wrist bone with a true contact shadow where the coil touches the skin; field about 35 cm wide, so the forearm is about a sixth of the frame width and the coil a little wider than the forearm. (Last time the wire came out about 7 mm thick, nearly twice too chunky: the two turns read about 14 mm and the coil looked narrower than the arm it goes round.) WORLD: a terrace wall, 21 December, 4:29 in the afternoon. THE SHADOW: the forearm's shadow falls on the wall to its right, an ordinary arm and hand, except the shadow wrist wears a whole stack: exactly twelve slim bangles climbing from the wrist to mid-forearm, each a thin crisp separate ring no thicker than the real coil's wire, with a sliver of light between it and the next, so all twelve rings can be counted on the shadow arm (last time only eight or nine could be counted). The real arm wears only the one two-turn coil. A real cast shadow in the same sun: same direction, deep warm cocoa brown, darker and browner than the saffron wall, never rust orange and never black, the plaster texture visible through it, razor-sharp at the piece and softening with distance; nothing else casts it, only the arm and its one bangle. LIGHT: soft open-sky fill from above and in front keeps the shadow side readable; one small hard specular kicker, the low December sun from the left, 10 degrees up, draws a crisp specular edge along the ribbed coil, one white catchlight per stone, and throws every shadow long to the right. FRAME: arm and shadow arm together centred: the forearm rises from the bottom edge just right of centre, the fingers leave the top edge, the coil a little above the middle of the frame height; the shadow arm along the right edge; the whole left 40 percent of the frame is calm empty wall from top to bottom, for the headline and the card; no part of the hand, thumb or arm enters the left 40 percent. Warm-neutral 18k gold tone, never brassy, orange or rose. Film grain, believable imperfection, a slow winter afternoon on an Indian terrace, editorial jewellery campaign. Real skin, no retouching. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no graffiti; no face, no eyes, no eyebrows anywhere, and no eyes or facial features in any silhouette; one bangle only: no rings, no watch, no henna. No water, no props. Never a grey, white, black or beige backdrop.
